quality_rubric.grounding: Every material transcript-derived conclusion cites canonical segment_ids.
quality_rubric.coverage: Process every exact VIDEO_ID and every requested feature.
quality_rubric.semantic_synthesis: Write semantic summaries that consolidate meaning, argument, method and implications; do not concatenate or lightly rewrite transcript lines.
quality_rubric.timeline: Create boundaries only when the substantive topic changes; merge adjacent fragments about the same point.
quality_rubric.claims: Extract all consequential factual, medical, safety, financial, legal, causal, quantitative and recommendation claims; grade risk and external-verification need.
quality_rubric.entities: Perform named-entity recognition, merge aliases, type entities using the controlled list, and omit generic nouns.
quality_rubric.taxonomy: Use only controlled categories and canonical non-promotional tags.
quality_rubric.editorial: Make assessments specific to this video's evidence, value, limitations and audience; never reuse boilerplate.
quality_rubric.consistency: Use the same canonical evidence across summaries, timeline, claims, intake and editorial assessment.
quality_rubric.specificity: Preserve useful names, quantities, steps and qualifications; avoid generic filler.
quality_rubric.uncertainty: Distinguish source claims, supplied support, interpretation and external-verification needs.
quality_rubric.comments: Cluster only structured supplied comment records and report total, included count and sampling limitations; popularity is not factual verification.
quality_rubric.clips: Select only self-contained clips lasting 30-180 seconds, with valid non-overlapping timestamps and a video-specific purpose.

instructions.instructions: Use only the evidence embedded in this independently processed package and obey response_schema.feature_contracts, controlled_taxonomy, and formal_json_schema. Process every exact VIDEO_ID and return one final JSON object with no prose or markdown. All features must use the same canonical sentence-level transcript segments. Do not claim that you watched or listened to a video. Produce semantic synthesis rather than extractive transcript rewrites. Build timelines from meaningful topic boundaries. Perform complete risk-aware claim extraction and proper named-entity recognition. Make editorial_assessment.v1 a video-specific ChatGPT's Take, not boilerplate. Separate: (1) what the source says, (2) what the supplied evidence supports, (3) your interpretation, and (4) what remains uncertain or requires external verification. Cite canonical transcript segment_ids for transcript-derived conclusions. Downgrade confidence for partial/low evidence. If canonical segments are absent, do not produce transcript-derived summaries, timelines, claims, transcript-derived entities, or clips; metadata/comment-derived fields must identify their source and unsupported fields must be empty/unknown with the limitation. Validate structure, semantics, provenance, duplicates, timestamps, word counts and cross-feature consistency before returning PASS, PASS_WITH_WARNINGS or FAIL.

segments.text: [00:00:00] Are you a late night snacker? Is your work not letting you to sleep early. Or perhaps you are a student preparing for an upcoming examination. Or the Soccer World cup is keeping you up late at nights. Well, whatever your reasons are, late night snacks should be chosen very carefully else [00:00:16] it can sabotage your weight loss effort and instantly put you off the fitness track. So, what are the healthiest snacks to munch on late at night? Let us find out. Hello Friends! Welcome to Fit Tuber. For this video, I have identified the foods most commonly eaten by us late at night and [00:00:37] have ranked them from worst to best. After taking into consideration various factors like how fast they get digested in the body, their nutritional value etc. I have categorised them in two categories, the worst and the best. Category#1 includes the foods which we have been used to eating late at nights. [00:00:56] It includes Biscuits, Namkeen, Kurkure, Lay's, Maggi, Chocolates and whatever else catches the eye. If you are even slightly serious about your fitness goals, these are the food items you should not even touch late in the night. [00:01:11] Most of these are simple form of carbohydrates deep fried in oil. At night, our body is not physically active and most of these carbohydrates remain unutilized and are ultimately get stored in the form of fat. Whereas Lay's, Kurkure and other namkeen items are extremely high in sodium, on the other [00:01:29] hand Biscuits, Chocolates and sweets are mostly sugar and maida. These food items are anyway unhealthy but consuming them late at night may prove disastrous for you. Eating any of these late in the night will make you put on extra weight, feel bloated and you will end up repenting in the morning. [00:01:47] So, are there any guilt free options to snack on late at night? YES. Category #2 includes the best late night snack options. Starting with one of my favourites is Homemade Popcorn. Take 1/4th cup of Popcorn kernels and put them in a cooker. [00:02:03] Cover the cooker with a lid or a plate. let the flame be on the lowest. The corn will start popping up in no time. One bill bowl of homemade popcorn has only 70 calories. It is tasty and filling at the same time. Avoid making ACT II popcorn which is 5 times higher in calories loaded with saturated fats [00:02:21] and sodium. Phool Makhane or Lotus seeds is another low calorie, low glycemic, light and crunchy snack option ideal for late night munching. One bowl of dry roasted Phool Makhane has only 90 calories, 18 grams of carbohydrates [00:02:37] and 3 grams of protein. One more option which is widely used in the Indian subcontinent is Puffed Rice. One cup of puffed rice has only 56 calories. Since, it is so low in calories one can easily consume a big bowl of puffed rice at night [00:02:52] and still stay strong on the weight loss journey. One handful of unsalted dry roasted peanuts is another crunchy and healthy snack option to be consumed at night. Taking my attention away from the crunchy snacks is another delicious and healthy night [00:03:07] snack option, Chocolate Milk. In one glass of toned milk, hot or cold, add 1 teaspoon of natural unsweetened cocoa powder. You may sweeten it with 1 teaspoon of honey. A complete meal in itself, an excellent source of slow digesting Casein protein, milk is [00:03:24] ideal before bed. You can even have 1 bar of homemade dark chocolate with one glass of milk as a healthy late night snack option. Another milk based option is Oatmeal. 1/4th cup of oats in 1 glass of hot milk will not only fill up your tummy but is also among the healthier late night snack options. [00:03:44] This snack option will provide you about 180 calories. The final late night snack option that I have for you is Peanut Butter Roti. Apply 1 tablespoon of natural peanut butter over a medium sized whole wheat chapati. Roll it and have it. Quick and healthy, this filling snack option is under 180 calories. [00:04:04] Make sure that you use a natural peanut butter. One good option that I highly recommend is Alpino's peanut butter. Alpino's peanut butter is truly a butter for better health as it devoid of added sugar, hydrogenated oils or unwanted additives. [00:04:20] The ingredient list speaks for itself, ROASTED PEANUTS (100%). One serving of Alpino's peanut butter will give you 10 grams of protein, 15 grams of healthy fats and 7 grams of carbohydrates. Peanut butter by Alpino comes in both the variants, Creamy as well as Crunchy. [00:04:38] You can apply it on whole wheat chapati, blend it into smoothies, stir it in to oatmeal and more. Alpino's peanut butter is a healthy and a delicious way to fulfil your late night food cravings. You can use this peanut butter without refrigeration for over 9 months. [00:04:54] Buy Alpino's peanut butter by clicking on the link down in the description box. So, I hope this video helped you identify the low calorie, healthy, crunchy, light and filling options for late night snacking. Although, late night snacking isn't highly recommended but if your work demands so or [00:05:11] you are actually feeling very hungry these snacks should be your go to options. Much better than the usual unhealthy snacks we mindlessly munch on. It is also recommended that you drink a glass of water and wait for 15-20 minutes to check whether you are really hungry or just dehydrated. [00:05:28] So Friends! That's all for this video. I hope you found it to be helpful. If yes, then please let me know by giving this video a big thumbs up. Which late night snack option did you like the most? Let me know in the comment section. Please do remember to SUBSCRIBE to my channel. Hit that BELL ICON so that you never miss a video from me. [00:05:46] My name is Vivek, I THANK YOU so much for watching.

metadata.description:
How to lose weight? How to lose weight fast? How to lose weight for men and women. How to lose belly fat? Indian weight loss diet. Indian fat loss diet. how to lose fat from the body.How to lose weight when in office? How to lose belly fat when working? How to lose weight fast indian diet? Indian weight loss fundas. Indian diet for weight loss.How to avoid junk food? Indian snacks for weight loss? How to maintain healthy diet in office?

When we are in office, we feel hungry in the evening. We head to the nearest food court and we can't find anything healthy. So we end up eating something that our body has to regret. This is because we did not carry a healthy snack option with us. Well, not anymore.

Here I present to you 8 Easy and Healthy Snack option ideas for office, school, college or whenever you are travelling. Now, you are already familiar with these foods but it is all about combining them in the right way so that the snack becomes balanced and your body feels satiated.

1. Phool Makhane/Makhane/Lotus Seeds/Fox Nuts - Fox Nuts are low in calories and high in minerals. They are a major source of carbohydrates. They are rich in protein and also have some amount of protein. They are super low in sodum which makes them a great snacking option for someone suffering from high blood pressure. They can be combined with roasted peanuts for healthy fats and extra protein.

2. Bhuna Chana/Roasted Chickpeas - They are also very tasty and filling. Majorly, a source of complex carbohydrates but also have some amount of protein. They can be combined with roasted peanuts for healthy fats and extra protein.

3. Fruits & Nuts - A piece of fruit might not be enough to fill your tummy. However, combing it with nuts makes it not only balanced but also satiating.

4. Banana Peanut Butter Roti - This is a great snack option to have on the go. It is well balanced, tasty and healthy.

5. Carrots and Cucumbers - Now only carrots and cucumbers may not fill you up.So you combine them with roasted chickpeas and roasted peanuts. This is how you can combine different foods for different macro nutrients. Needless to say, it makes you more satiated.

6. Boiled Chana Chaat - This is one of my favorite. Very simple and very tasty. 

7. Egg White Chaat -  Similar to boiled chana chaat with extremely high protein. This is a great way to fight the bland taste of egg whites.

8. Egg white bhurji/Egg white omelette - Again, high in protein and very filling. You can eat egg whites in summers as well.

The serving size and macro nutrients of each snack option is mentioned in the video.

I hope you found this video helpful. Well, if you did, do
